title: Dry eye testing
what: The doctor checks how many tears your eyes make and how long they stay on the surface of the eye.
why: When your eyes feel dry, burn, turn red, feel gritty, or get tired from screens.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; the doctor tells you the result right away
tell_doctor: What eye drops and medicines you use
Long screen time or air conditioning
Past eye surgery, including laser vision correction

prepare.title: Drops
prepare.text: Ask the clinic whether to skip lubricating drops before the exam.

prepare.title: Lenses and makeup
prepare.text: Best to come without contacts and without eye makeup.

bring: A list of your eye drops and medicines
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
Your eyes are examined under a microscope
A dye may be put in to see how fast the tear film breaks up
Sometimes a paper strip is placed under the lower lid for 5 minutes
The strip shows how many tears you make
feel: The strip under the lid tickles a little, and you want to blink
The dye may turn your tears yellow for a while
after: Your eyes may water for a few minutes
The doctor will suggest care and eye drops

faq.q: Why do my eyes get dry?
faq.a: Often from screens, dry air, age, contact lenses, or medicines. Your doctor will help find the cause.

faq.q: Can I use lubricating drops all the time?
faq.a: Many are fine, but ask your doctor which ones and how often.

reminders.text: Dry eye test tomorrow. Come without contacts and eye makeup if you can.
